## Current Code Workflow (from code analyzer)
# Model Overview (for Diagnosis)

The probe uses item embeddings and sequence features through a SASRec-compatible interface. `item_emb.weight` supplies item vectors; `log2feats(sequence)` computes features at each sequence position; `predict_score(features, items)` scores positive and negative items. The model implementation is absent, so the internal encoder and final user-representation extraction cannot be established. Diagnosis evaluates features across valid positions, rather than explicitly selecting the final sequence representation.

# Diagnosis Inputs & Hooks

`DiagnosisProbe(model, device)` receives the compatibility view and stores its metadata, review data, and training histories. Reviews and histories are not subsequently used. Training batches contain `(None, sequence, positive, negative)` with shape B × L. The probe converts sequences to NumPy, obtains sequence features, and scores stacked positive/negative candidates under evaluation mode without gradients.

# Probes & Metrics

- **Embedding collapse:** Excludes padding item 0, samples up to 2,048 item embeddings using seed 42, normalizes them, and averages off-diagonal cosine similarities. Mapping this mean through `(cosine + 1)/2` yields the collapse score. Higher indicates greater directional alignment; approximately 0.5 represents zero average cosine similarity. This does not directly measure recommendation diversity.
- **Positive–negative separation:** Processes at most ten training batches, excluding positions whose positive item is 0. Computes `positive_logit − negative_logit`, reporting its mean, lower tenth percentile, fraction below zero, and fraction below 0.5. Higher margins and lower failure fractions generally indicate stronger training-pair separation.
- **Category breakdown:** Counts category occurrences separately for positive and negative items in weak-margin and wrong-rank cases, retaining the top twenty categories. These are raw counts, not normalized error rates. Categories are unavailable in this benchmark, so breakdown lists should be empty.

# Perturbation & Tests

No sequence shuffling, input perturbation, sensitivity testing, or SVD analysis occurs. Random embedding subsampling controls probe cost; it is not a robustness test.

# MODEL_DIAGNOSIS Schema & Limitations

`run_full_diagnosis` returns `metrics` and `metric_definitions`. Metrics contain five scalar measurements and a nested category breakdown with thresholds, totals, and category counts. Empty margin samples produce zeros, potentially resembling healthy failure rates.

`diagnosis_interpreter_prompt` embeds these measurements and definitions into a prompt requesting JSON with `status`, `core_findings`, `key_implications`, and `evidence`; it does not itself generate the interpretation. Diagnosis does not measure validation HR@10, generalization, full-catalog recommendation quality, or unobserved simulator traits.

the diagnostic interpretation prompt using measured metrics and their definitions.
view.model is the actual trained nn.Module. view.item_emb, log2feats(sequence),
predict_score(features, items), user_train, meta_data, review_data implement the
initial SASRec compatibility contract. Adapt probes when changing the architecture.
train_loader yields (None, sequence, positive, negative), tensors of shape B x L.
Only public interaction histories, item titles, descriptions and timestamps are available.
Review ratings/text, item ratings/categories/prices/stores are NOT available in this
shared RecHarness task. Never invent them. Simulator diversity/conformity traits are
explicitly unobserved. Twenty real training users (five/category) receive full-catalog
unseen-item recommendations, as the native simulator requires. Selection uses the
common macro validation HR@10, replacing the native HR@5/NDCG@5 combined score.

## Current Code Workflow (from code analyzer)
# Model Overview (for Diagnosis)

The probe uses item embeddings and sequence features through a SASRec-compatible interface. `item_emb.weight` supplies item vectors; `log2feats(sequence)` computes features at each sequence position; `predict_score(features, items)` scores positive and negative items. The model implementation is absent, so the internal encoder and final user-representation extraction cannot be established. Diagnosis evaluates features across valid positions, rather than explicitly selecting the final sequence representation.

# Diagnosis Inputs & Hooks

`DiagnosisProbe(model, device)` receives the compatibility view and stores its metadata, review data, and training histories. Reviews and histories are not subsequently used. Training batches contain `(None, sequence, positive, negative)` with shape B × L. The probe converts sequences to NumPy, obtains sequence features, and scores stacked positive/negative candidates under evaluation mode without gradients.

# Probes & Metrics

- **Embedding collapse:** Excludes padding item 0, samples up to 2,048 item embeddings using seed 42, normalizes them, and averages off-diagonal cosine similarities. Mapping this mean through `(cosine + 1)/2` yields the collapse score. Higher indicates greater directional alignment; approximately 0.5 represents zero average cosine similarity. This does not directly measure recommendation diversity.
- **Positive–negative separation:** Processes at most ten training batches, excluding positions whose positive item is 0. Computes `positive_logit − negative_logit`, reporting its mean, lower tenth percentile, fraction below zero, and fraction below 0.5. Higher margins and lower failure fractions generally indicate stronger training-pair separation.
- **Category breakdown:** Counts category occurrences separately for positive and negative items in weak-margin and wrong-rank cases, retaining the top twenty categories. These are raw counts, not normalized error rates. Categories are unavailable in this benchmark, so breakdown lists should be empty.

# Perturbation & Tests

No sequence shuffling, input perturbation, sensitivity testing, or SVD analysis occurs. Random embedding subsampling controls probe cost; it is not a robustness test.

# MODEL_DIAGNOSIS Schema & Limitations

`run_full_diagnosis` returns `metrics` and `metric_definitions`. Metrics contain five scalar measurements and a nested category breakdown with thresholds, totals, and category counts. Empty margin samples produce zeros, potentially resembling healthy failure rates.

`diagnosis_interpreter_prompt` embeds these measurements and definitions into a prompt requesting JSON with `status`, `core_findings`, `key_implications`, and `evidence`; it does not itself generate the interpretation. Diagnosis does not measure validation HR@10, generalization, full-catalog recommendation quality, or unobserved simulator traits.
